pages.title: Agent Runtime and LLM Integration
pages.purpose: How an agent turn runs: chat loop in agent.ts, executeCode sandbox and tool surface, model provider registry (ai-models.ts), pi-based invocation (ai-invoke.ts), prompt compaction, slash commands, and daily usage limits.
instructions: Cover model choice, BYOK, and gateway routing as implemented, not as marketed.
Describe Code Mode: the agent acts by writing/executing snippets; ground in the executeCode path.

pages.title: Backend Kernel (workshop-backend)
pages.purpose: The workshop-backend worker: server.ts entry and RPC root, session token scheme, UserDurableObject as the per-user state owner, AdminSettings DO, PendingLogin, DO migrations, and auth enforcement chokepoints.
instructions: Explain the token format and where it is verified.
Focus on ownership: what lives in the User DO vs the Overseer DO vs KV.

pages.title: Blueprints and Output Formats
pages.purpose: Blueprint sharing: what is captured vs not, binding annotations, the Gadget DO -> User DO -> KV propagation and R2 content store, export/import archives, and the deployment-shipped format blueprints pipeline.
instructions: Explain the blueprintId stability constraint and the generator's cache-avoidance behavior.
docs/blueprints.md is descriptive; verify against blueprint-archive.ts before claiming storage details.

pages.title: Gadget Runtime: Sandboxes, Code Storage, Editing
pages.purpose: How a gadget exists and runs: server facet in a Dynamic Worker with no internet except bindings, client iframe with postMessage RPC, Yjs code-change merging (code-change.ts), git-store persistence, and typed-storage collections.
instructions: Cover conflict merging and commit flow at a mechanism level.
Explain the client/server split of a gadget and how bindings gate outbound access.

pages.title: Overseer: The Workspace Durable Object
pages.purpose: OverseerDurableObject responsibilities: chats, workpieces/gadgets as facets, named bindings, gatekeeper facet installation, hooks/loopback, workspace outputs, and the Overseer RPC surface implementation.
instructions: State uncertainty where behavior is not verifiable from the file alone.
overseer.ts is ~11k lines; explain the major subsystems by name and line region rather than exhaustive coverage.

pages.title: System Architecture Overview
pages.purpose: The mental model: Cloudflare OS as an OS (kernel=workshop-backend, drivers=gatekeepers, shell=frontend, processes=gadgets), package map, and the end-to-end request/data flow from browser through router to overseer, gadget facets, and gatekeepers.
instructions: Ground the OS analogy table in actual code paths where possible.
Trace one representative flow (open a chat, run an agent turn, call a gatekeeper) across packages.

pages.title: RPC Contract (workshop-shared)
pages.purpose: How client and server speak Cap'n Web RPC: PublicApi/AuthenticatedApi/Overseer surfaces in api.ts, the gatekeeper interface family in gatekeeper.ts, promise pipelining, @validateRpc runtime validation, stub disposal, and the useState-with-stubs pitfall.
instructions: Cite specific interface declarations for each claim about semantics.
Describe the API boundary semantics (interfaces as capabilities), not a method-by-method dump.

pages.title: Build System and Toolchain
pages.purpose: How this workspace builds: pnpm + Vite+ (vp) tasks and the task cache, env declaration rules, why no baseUrl/incremental, singleThreaded tsgo, lint via vp/oxlint, codegen tasks (format blueprints, configurators, worker types), and the gotchas catalog from AGENTS.md verified in configs.
instructions: Keep this about the build toolchain, not tests (testing page owns test tasks except shared config plumbing).
Verify each AGENTS.md claim against the actual configs; AGENTS.md is a secondary source.

pages.title: Testing Strategy and Harnesses
pages.purpose: The test layers: node --test script suites, per-package vitest (node vs workerd projects), assert-workerd guard, with-timeout watchdog, cached test tasks, golden files, contribution-policy test, and the out-of-process integration-tests harness with its fixture gatekeeper.
instructions: Cover the fresh-identity convention for storage isolation.
Explain why fake timers cannot work in the integration harness and what replaces them.

pages.title: Change Guide: Adding a Gatekeeper
pages.purpose: A focused maintenance walkthrough for a new gatekeeper worker: package skeleton from an existing one, implementing Vendor/User/Session, OAuth + resource configurators, auto-provisioning option, router binding (zero-code install), deploy inputs, and test hooks.
instructions: Ground each step in files that already exist in an example package rather than inventing steps.
The repo's own write-gatekeeper skill is evidence of intended practice; cite it as a pointer, don't paraphrase wholesale.

pages.title: Change Guide: Modifying the RPC API
pages.purpose: A focused maintenance walkthrough: add or change a method in workshop-shared api.ts, implement it in workshop-backend without hand-written mirror interfaces, wire a frontend caller, run the right validation, and respect the review rules for the kernel and shared API.
instructions: Include the doc-comment and @validateRpc requirements and the pipelining/disposal rules as checklist items.
Show the concrete edit points a real change touches, using a plausible example grounded in an existing method pair (interface + Impl).

pages.title: Context Library and Scheduler
pages.purpose: The two auto-provisioned singleton gatekeepers: gatekeeper-context (three DOs, sharingDomain isolation, private/public collections, agent read session, observations) and gatekeeper-scheduler (ScheduleDriver DO, alarm delivery, ambient singleton bindings).
instructions: Explain the autoProvisionsAccount + singleton + ambient binding path end to end using these two as the concrete cases.

pages.title: Gatekeeper Implementations Catalog
pages.purpose: Survey of shipped gatekeepers: representative architectures (github, google, email, notion, slack, spotify, zoominfo, homeassistant, confluence, linear, supabase), each one's OAuth setup requirements, and what binds them together (each has a README for vendor app config).
instructions: Cite each package's README for vendor-config claims.
Do not narrate every file; identify 2-3 genuinely different implementation shapes (OAuth API proxy, resource resolver, non-OAuth auto-provisioner).

pages.title: Gatekeeper Framework
pages.purpose: The shared gatekeeper architecture: GatekeeperVendor -> connected GatekeeperUser -> per-resource Gatekeeper DO; connect callback and OAuth handling; resource-URL scope grammar; Observation/ActionDescription contracts; configurator UIs; hooks; and the loopback entrypoints used for facet access.
instructions: Document the Gatekeeper* interface family precisely: which side implements what.
Use github as the canonical worked example but keep the page about the framework contracts.

pages.title: MCP Connectors (mcp-shared, mcp, mcp-portal)
pages.purpose: The two MCP gatekeepers and their shared library: endpoint vs portal trust model, scope grammar in resource URLs, queued actions store, OAuth via the official SDK, and the tools.ts trust boundary with readOnlyHint and vetted-endpoint auto-apply.
instructions: Check mcp-shared README against src before asserting behaviors.
Explain precisely why only portal endpoints can produce vetted annotations.

pages.title: Configuration and Admin Settings
pages.purpose: The full configuration surface: backend/gatekeeper env vars, AdminConfig ownership (AdminSettings DO + .adminConfig KV mirror), provisioning modes for auto-provisioning gatekeepers, feature flags, AI Gateway billing enablement, and site branding.
instructions: Separate env-var config from admin-panel config explicitly (the security rationale matters).
Summarize the three-state provisioning policy resolution from source.

pages.title: Logging, Observability, and Error Reporting
pages.purpose: How failures become visible: backend-utils logger conventions and typed fields, observability context, reportIssue to the optional external Reporter, the frontend error-reporting package and the /api/client-errors endpoint, and gatekeeper iframe postMessage reporting.
instructions: Distinguish server-side reporting from the opt-in frontend path.
Document the no-secrets rules and the unverified reportedUserId caveat as invariants.

pages.title: Router, Release Pipeline, and Preview Deploys
pages.purpose: How code reaches an instance: the router worker's binding-discovered routing, scripts/release build/upload/promote flow, manifest placeholders and golden test, R2 content addressing, and the preview deploy scripts.
instructions: Cover why promotion is a single manifest copy and what CI serialization protects.
Explain deploy-inputs.json and NO_DEFAULT_CRED_INPUTS.

pages.title: Authentication and Sign-in
pages.purpose: All sign-in paths: username/password (client-side argon2id with SERVICE_SALT), OAuth via authentication gatekeepers (AUTH_GATEKEEPERS, PendingLogin, transient minimal grants), Cloudflare Access mode, and how auth config is env-driven by design.
instructions: Explain the email-keyed identity invariant and why auth config is NOT in AdminConfig.
Verify doc claims against auth/ source before repeating them.

pages.title: Capability Security Model
pages.purpose: The security core: capability-based introductions, observations as audit/authorization units, approval queue with action simulation, lockdown/prohibitAllSharing, ambient vs bound access, and where each check is enforced.
instructions: Distinguish the three enforcement points: gatekeeper DO, overseer, and admin chokepoints.
Explain the async approval design (simulate now, approve later) and its invariants.

pages.title: Sharing and Observer Enforcement
pages.purpose: Collaboration security: share links vs explicit users, build/use roles, observer registration with per-gatekeeper verification via GatekeeperUserVerifier, forward exclusion, and re-check on open.
instructions: Cover the ObserverConfigCallback flow used by openGadget.
docs/observers.md is a historical plan: verify the implemented surface against sharing.ts and overseer.ts.

pages.title: Quickstart
pages.purpose: Practical entry point: install/build/run locally (pnpm run-local), split dev loop (dev-server + dev-client), what to try in the UI, package tour, and how to build/test/lint.
instructions: Give exact commands and ports as found in scripts, not generic advice.
Note what run-local builds vs what it skips, per scripts/run-local.ts comments.
